sections.html: Corydoras imitator is currently imported from the upper Rio Negro in Brazil.

On close inspection of the imported fish, hardly two specimens look identical. Coloration is variable, as is the shape of the body. Some fish are certainly unplanned by-catches, for example C. incolicana (C1). However, it seems very doubtful that Corydoras imitator (with a quite narrow black band on the back) and C39 (with a more robust body and a much broader band on the back that reaches the lower plate-row of the body in the region of the tail fin) really represent two different species. At least both forms are collected and exported together, and there are so many intermediate individuals that it is impossible to sort them properly.
